content.title: What we learned running Pulse 2026
content.excerpt: 2,400 people, 58 talks and one very long coffee queue. Here is what we are changing for 2027.
content.content:
Pulse 2026 sold out three weeks early. We read every one of the 1,100 feedback forms; these are the changes they asked for.

Shorter talks, longer breaks

Most talks move from 45 to 40 minutes, and every break is now 30 minutes. The hallway track is half the reason people come.

A second stage for workshops

Workshops sold out in a day, so 12 May becomes a full workshop day at LX Factory with eight rooms.

The best conference I have been to in years — and I finally met the people behind the tools I use every day.

Attendee survey, 2026

content.title: How to get the most out of a two-day conference
content.excerpt: Pick two talks a day, plan one conversation, and leave room for the unplanned.
content.content:
Two days goes fast. The people who get the most out of Pulse plan a little and leave room for a lot.

  • Mark two must-see talks per day in the app; let the rest find you.
  • Write down one question you want answered by Friday.
  • Sit somewhere new at lunch — every table is mixed on purpose.
  • Use the quiet rooms. Nobody does their best thinking in a crowd.

And go to the after-party, even for an hour. Half of next year's speakers were in the audience the year before.

content.title: Announcing the 2027 workshop programme
content.excerpt: Eight hands-on workshops on 12 May, from AI agents to design tokens. Seats are capped at 24.
content.content:
Workshops are four hours, hands-on and capped at 24 seats so every attendee gets time with the instructor.

  • Designing with AI agents — Mei Lin Chen
  • Design tokens from Figma to code — Amara Okafor
  • Edge functions in practice — Rohan Mehta
  • Running a research sprint — Omar Haddad

Workshop seats come with the Conference + Workshop pass. Pick your workshop after checkout.
